notes: This registry is the canonical queue for serious experiments.
Create an experiment folder only when the run actually starts.
Keep stable prep artifacts in ../derived, not here.
Current next-step decision tree is in docs/norgesgruppen-data/plans/PLAN-0003-critical-path-and-decision-tree-after-preflight.md.

experiments.question: Can we reproduce the blocked validation split and compute the canonical bucketed competition-proxy metrics locally?
experiments.success_gate: One command produces primary metrics, bucketed metrics, and a fixed-format error report for a saved prediction file.
experiments.result_note: Implemented scripts/eval_norgesgruppen_predictions.py and passed empty/oracle sanity cases.

experiments.question: What is the floor for GT-crop recognition before using stronger embedders?
experiments.success_gate: Strict, extended, and full recognition slices all produce sane non-random baselines and error reports.
experiments.result_note: Implemented scripts/benchmark_norgesgruppen_crops.py. Hash nearest-neighbor beats random on strict/extended/full; egg and low-view buckets remain extremely weak; full slice has 199 unevaluable queries.

experiments.question: How strong is PE-Core as the primary catalog retrieval embedder on GT crops?
experiments.success_gate: Clearly beats EXP-0002 on strict-slice top-1, Recall@5, and macro top-1.
experiments.result_note: PE-Core decisively cleared the floor. Strict top-1 0.627952 vs hash 0.068176, strict mAP@20 0.721652 vs 0.108862. Full evaluable fraction stayed 0.954814, so remaining misses are mostly structural no-reference buckets and sibling-variant confusion.

experiments.question: How strong is DINOv3 as a pure-vision retrieval embedder on GT crops?
experiments.success_gate: Either beats PE-Core on a meaningful slice or provides complementary confusion behavior worth fusion.
experiments.result_note: Public timm DINOv3 was much worse than PE-Core. Strict top-1 0.246409 vs PE-Core 0.627952. Oracle union with PE-Core only reaches 0.661066 on strict, so complementarity exists but is too small to justify DINOv3 as the main path.

experiments.question: After retrieval plus classifier fallback, does OCR materially reduce the remaining sibling-SKU confusion?
experiments.success_gate: Improves strict-slice recognition and sibling-heavy / low-view buckets without hurting overall calibration.

experiments.question: What is the fastest submission-friendly class-agnostic localization baseline?
experiments.success_gate: Overfit sanity passes and blocked-split class-agnostic AP50 is strong enough to anchor later pipeline work.
experiments.result_note: Detector lane is now real, not just unblocked. After fixing env drift and passing 4-image overfit sanity at mAP50 0.78879 / mAP50-95 0.59923, the 10-epoch YOLOv8n blocked-val baseline reached canonical class-agnostic AP50 0.852028, AP75 0.530942, mAP50-95 0.494438, miss rate 0.048592, and count MAE 31.306122. That is a large jump over the 1-epoch smoke and makes YOLOv8n the current localization anchor.

experiments.question: Does RF-DETR materially improve localization over YOLOv8 in this dense shelf regime?
experiments.success_gate: Beats EXP-0006 on class-agnostic AP50 and count MAE without unacceptable complexity.

experiments.question: Does the decomposition stack already beat simple closed-set baselines end-to-end?
experiments.success_gate: Hybrid proxy beats the simplest monolithic baseline and failures are understandable by bucket.
experiments.result_note: The first real detector + retrieval stack is now measured on blocked val. Using the 10-epoch YOLOv8n detector filtered at min_score 0.4, detector-only hybrid is 0.557981 while detector + PE-Core reaches classification mAP50 0.452121 and hybrid 0.693615. Same-box oracle-class bound is 0.817538, so decomposition works but current recognizer/calibration leaves material headroom. Matched true-positive detector crops show top-1/top-5 0.627225 / 0.825916 overall and 0.658966 / 0.867712 on reference-like buckets. Cheap score fusion using detector_score * retrieval_top1_score already improves hybrid to 0.717616, making calibration and classifier fallback the next main path.

experiments.question: How competitive is a simple monolithic multi-class detector as an ablation?
experiments.success_gate: Provides a fair closed-set reference for stack-vs-monolith decisions.

experiments.question: Can the best practical baseline be packaged into a sandbox-compatible submission path early?
experiments.success_gate: Local submission-style run works with realistic latency and artifact-size checks.

experiments.question: What end-to-end competition-proxy score does current PE-Core retrieval reach if localization is perfect?
experiments.success_gate: Produce a trustworthy image-level upper bound using GT boxes, saved PE-Core rankings, and real cache-derived similarity scores.
experiments.result_note: Oracle-box PE-Core bound landed at hybrid 0.860238 with detection AP50 ignore-class 1.0 and classification mAP50 0.534127. This proves localization is worth serious work, but retrieval-only recognition still has structural zeros in missing-reference, sibling-trap, and unknown_sentinel buckets.

experiments.question: How far can the first real detector carry the hybrid score if classification after detection were perfect?
experiments.success_gate: Produce a trustworthy localization upper bound that isolates post-detector recognition headroom from detector recall limits.
experiments.result_note: The initial 1-epoch read yielded hybrid 0.749827, but the latest canonical rerun on the 10-epoch YOLOv8n baseline reached detector-box oracle-class hybrid 0.879192 with detection AP50 0.852028 and classification mAP50 0.942574. Compared with perfect-box PE-Core hybrid 0.860238, this means localization is no longer obviously the single largest remaining limiter; real pipeline recognition work is now justified.

experiments.question: Can a shelf-crop closed-set classifier recover the no-reference, sentinel, and shelf-domain cases that retrieval cannot solve well?
experiments.success_gate: Improves full-slice and hard-bucket recognition, especially missing-reference, unknown_sentinel, and low-view regimes, without collapsing strong reference-safe classes.
experiments.result_note: Classifier lane is now real. Direct frozen PE-Core linear-probe controls are clean: held-out tiny best val top-1 0.8125, paired shuffled-label best top-1 0.25 / final 0.15625, and same-sample exact-crop memorization 1.0 / 1.0 by epoch 3. Cached exact-crop route is now trusted too: cached held-out tiny best top-1 0.78125, cached same-sample memorization 1.0 / 1.0 by epoch 9, and resume smoke proved split-level reuse works. Quick CPU cache benchmark showed 256/0 only marginally faster than 128/0, so 128/0 is the safer first full-run config. Next step is the first full cached GT-crop baseline on train-all -> val-all.

experiments.question: Does detector plus retrieval plus classifier fallback materially beat retrieval-only end-to-end and become the first serious submission candidate?
experiments.success_gate: Beats the detector-plus-retrieval stack on hybrid proxy and specifically fixes structural full-slice failures without unacceptable complexity.
